title: Limbus-to-Cornea: Masterclass in Limbal Stem Cell Deficiency (LSCD)
summary: Limbal Stem Cell Deficiency (LSCD) is a profound ocular surface pathology resulting from the loss or dysfunction of the limbal stem cell niche, leading to conjunctivalization, chronic inflammation, and vision loss. This infographic synthesizes the latest in regenerative medicine and clinical management.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: LSCD occurs when the limbal stem cell population (located in the Palisades of Vogt) is depleted, exhausted, or rendered dysfunctional. The primary barrier to conjunctival cell migration is lost, allowing conjunctival epithelium (goblet cells) to migrate onto the corneal surface, resulting in vascularization, scarring, and persistent epithelial defects.

sections.title: Clinical Features Checklist
content: Loss of limbal palisades of Vogt

sections.title: Red Flags: When to refer for Surgery
content: Intractable ocular pain (glaucoma or surface nerve exposure)
Rapid centripetal progression of conjunctival pannus

sections.title: Investigations Workup
content: 1. Slit-lamp exam: Look for loss of Palisades of Vogt
2. Impression Cytology: Gold standard (look for goblet cells)
3. In-vivo Confocal Microscopy (IVCM): Identify basal cell density
5. Anterior Segment OCT: Measure corneal epithelial thickness

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: 1. Optimize surface: Preservative-free ATs + Scleral lenses
2. Address Ocular Surface inflammation: Topical steroids/CsA
